idiom_name: length-prefixed hop records in a counted header field (MQTT v5 user properties or an AMQP table entry)
implementation_notes: C has no message abstraction and no header type, so the classic structure becomes an explicit wire layout: reserve one header field (an MQTT v5 USER_PROPERTY via Paho's MQTTProperties, an AMQP 0.9.1 table entry, or the first frame of a custom protocol) and append one length-prefixed record - component id plus timestamp - before republishing. The classic structure of a history container owned by a framework is replaced by hand-written helpers (append, parse, cap, copy) over a caller-owned buffer. Keep the parser strictly bounded: read the record length, validate it against the remaining bytes, and only then touch the payload; copy the buffer whenever a message is fanned out to several destinations.
pitfalls: Parsing an untrusted history: a length field from a partner must be validated against the remaining buffer before any read, otherwise the trail is a buffer-overflow vector.
Branch aliasing: with a heap buffer, two channels that share the same history_t will append into each other and can double-free; copy per branch.
No type system on the wire: the record layout, endianness and timestamp unit must be documented and versioned, or readers silently misinterpret partner entries.
